E2_rules.source_excerpt: “Pollution of air” refers to the undertaking’s emissions into air (both indoor and outdoor)... Phase 2 relates to the evaluation... including by assessing the severity and likelihood of impacts on the environment and human health.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show emissions or effluents of pollutants to water, especially in areas at water risk or high water stress, then an actual or potential negative impact from water pollution may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: emissions to water; effluents; water pollutants; wastewater discharge; pollutant loads; areas at water risk; high water stress; site-level water emissions
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Aquatic environment, human health, affected communities

impact_materiality.scale: Assess severity at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood for potential impacts at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the site, source, sector and geographic extent of water emissions, including the share occurring in areas at water risk or high water stress.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether water-pollution impacts can be prevented, controlled or reduced and whether affected ecosystems can be restored.

E2_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E2 paragraphs 4, 11(a); AR 5(b), AR 6, AR 23(c)
E2_rules.source_excerpt: “Pollution of water” refers to the undertaking’s emissions to water... [consider] the undertaking’s percentage of the total emissions of pollutants to water and soil occurring in areas at water risk.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show releases of pollutants into soil, contaminated sites, deposits, landfills, or environmental contamination at production or storage sites, then an actual or potential negative impact from soil pollution may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: emissions into soil; soil pollutants; contaminated sites; deposits; landfills; production sites; storage sites; land contamination; remediation
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Soil and ecosystems, human health, affected communities

impact_materiality.scale: Assess severity at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood for potential impacts at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the site, source, sector and geographic extent of soil emissions and contaminated production, storage or disposal sites.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess the feasibility of rehabilitating contaminated sites, recultivating landfills and removing contamination at production or storage sites.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: “Pollution of soil” refers to the undertaking’s emissions into soil... provisions for environmental protection and remediation costs, e.g., for rehabilitating contaminated sites.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that microplastics are generated, used, or procured during production, unintentionally produced through wear and tear, or leave facilities as emissions, products, or parts of products or services, then an actual or potential negative pollution impact may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: microplastics; production processes; procured microplastics; product ingredients; emissions; tire wear; synthetic textile wear; exfoliating beads; mixtures; articles
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Environment, marine and freshwater ecosystems, human health

impact_materiality.scale: Assess severity at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood for potential impacts at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the sites, sectors or business units and value-chain flows where microplastics are generated, used, procured or leave facilities.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether microplastic pollution can be prevented, controlled or reduced and whether affected ecosystems can be restored.

E2_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E2 paragraph 28(b); AR 4(a), AR 5(c), AR 20
E2_rules.source_excerpt: Microplastics may be unintentionally produced when larger pieces of plastics like car tires or synthetic textiles wear and tear or may be deliberately manufactured and added to products.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show the production, use, procurement, distribution, commercialisation, or import/export of substances of concern, whether alone, in mixtures, ingredients, semi-finished goods, or final products, then actual or potential negative impacts on health and the environment may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: substances of concern; hazardous substances; production; use; procurement; distribution; commercialisation; import/export; ingredients; mixtures; articles; products; emissions; hazard classes
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Human health, consumers and end-users, workers, affected communities, environment

impact_materiality.scale: Assess severity at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood for potential impacts at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the sites, sectors or business units and value-chain flows involving substances of concern, including own operations and procured substances.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether impacts can be prevented through substitution or minimisation of substances of concern and whether pollution-related ecosystem impacts can be restored.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: The objective... is to enable an understanding of the impact of the undertaking on health and the environment through substances of concern... substances in the undertaking’s own operations and those procured shall be included.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show the production, use, procurement, distribution, commercialisation, import/export, or presence in products of substances of very high concern, then actual or potential negative impacts on health and the environment may be relevant and should be considered separately.
E2_rules.identification_cues: substances of very high concern; SVHC; phase-out; non-essential use; consumer products; procured substances; mixtures; articles; product content; emissions
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Human health, consumers and end-users, workers, affected communities, environment

impact_materiality.scale: Assess severity at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood for potential impacts at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the sites, sectors or business units and value-chain flows involving substances of very high concern, including own operations and procured substances.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether impacts can be prevented through substitution, minimisation or phase-out of substances of very high concern and whether pollution-related ecosystem impacts can be restored.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: The undertaking shall present separately the information for substances of very high concern... [including] substances in the undertaking’s own operations and those procured.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show pollution incidents, deposits, emergency situations, or failures to avoid, control, or limit releases, then actual or potential negative impacts on people and the environment may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: pollution incident; emergency situation; accidental release; deposit; spill; breach; production interruption; uncontrolled emissions; impact limitation; environmental damage

impact_materiality.scale: Assess severity at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood for potential impacts at each material site or business unit, considering effects on the environment and human health.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the sites, operations and supply-chain activities involved and the extent of incident effects on people and the environment.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether incident effects can be controlled and limited and whether affected ecosystems can be restored, regenerated or transformed.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: [Policies address] avoiding incidents and emergency situations, and if and when they occur, controlling and limiting their impact on people and the environment.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show actions that restore, regenerate, or transform ecosystems where pollution has occurred, then an actual or potential positive environmental impact may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: ecosystem restoration; regeneration; transformation; polluted site restoration; contaminated-site rehabilitation; recultivation; environmental remediation

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the significance of the restoration, regeneration, or transformation for the affected ecosystem and environment.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood that planned restoration, regeneration, or transformation actions will produce the intended positive impact.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the extent of polluted ecosystems addressed across relevant sites and own operations or value-chain activities.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Not applicable in the same way as for negative impacts; assess whether the actions effectively restore, regenerate or transform ecosystems where pollution occurred.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: [Actions may] restore, regenerate and transform ecosystems where pollution has occurred... [The Standard covers] material positive and negative actual or potential impacts.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show exposure to new or changing pollution regulation, sanctions, litigation, negligence claims concerning ecosystems, enhanced reporting duties, permit breaches, or enforcement actions, then a pollution-related policy and legal risk may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: new regulation; sanctions; litigation; ecosystem negligence; reporting obligations; permit breach; non-compliance; enforcement action; IED; BAT; E-PRTR; fines; penalties

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects on financial position, financial performance, and cash flows, including fines, penalties, compliance costs, litigation, and remediation costs.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood of regulatory change, non-compliance, enforcement, sanctions, or litigation based on the undertaking’s activities and exposures.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: policy and legal: e.g., introduction of regulation, exposure to sanctions and litigation... enhanced reporting obligations.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that products, services, or processes may be substituted by lower-impact alternatives, or that the undertaking must transition away from substances of concern, then a pollution-related technology transition risk may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: product substitution; service substitution; lower-impact alternatives; transition away from substances of concern; phase-out; process redesign; clean technology; R&D requirements

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects from product or process replacement, research and development, capital expenditure, lost revenue, or asset adaptation.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood and timing of technological substitution or required transition away from substances of concern.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: technology: e.g., substitution of products or services by products or services with a lower impact, transition away from substances of concern.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show shifting supply, demand, or financing conditions, or volatility or increased costs for substances linked to pollution, then a pollution-related market transition risk may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: shifting supply; shifting demand; financing shifts; substance price volatility; increased substance costs; customer preferences; supplier availability; market restrictions

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects on revenue, input costs, financing, margins, financial position, and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood of relevant changes in supply, demand, financing, or substance prices and availability.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: market: e.g., shifting supply, demand and financing, volatility or increased costs of some substances.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show adverse or changing societal, customer, or community perceptions of the undertaking’s role in pollution prevention and control, then a pollution-related reputational risk may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: community opposition; customer concern; societal perception; pollution controversy; complaints; stakeholder criticism; reputation; pollution prevention performance
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Undertaking, customers, affected communities, wider society

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects on demand, stakeholder relationships, financing, financial performance, and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood of perception changes based on pollution impacts, incidents, controls, and stakeholder consultation.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: reputation: e.g., changing societal, customer or community perceptions as a result of an organisation’s role in pollution prevention and control.

E2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Pollution incidents and loss of clean resources
E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show sudden interruption of access to clean water, acid rain, or other pollution incidents that have caused or are likely to cause environmental and societal effects, then a pollution-related physical risk may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: clean-water interruption; acid rain; pollution incident; contaminated supply; operational disruption; environmental effects; societal effects; site exposure

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects from disruption, loss of resource access, remediation, compensation, and impacts on financial position, performance, and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood of incidents or interruptions using site, sector, and value-chain exposure.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: identify physical risks, e.g., sudden interruption of access to clean water, acid rain, or other pollution incidents.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show major pollution incidents, deposits, production interruptions, contaminated sites, remediation obligations, damage compensation, fines, penalties, or environmental provisions, then a pollution-related financial risk may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: major incident; deposit; production interruption; remediation provision; environmental protection costs; contaminated site; compensation; fines; penalties; capex; opex

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess operating and capital expenditure, provisions, compensation, fines, penalties, lost production, and effects on financial position, performance, and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood from incident history, deposits, site conditions, supply-chain interruptions, enforcement exposure, and remediation obligations.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: The operating and capital expenditures related to incidents and deposits may include... cost for eliminating and remediating... damage compensation costs including payment of fines and penalties.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show potential to decrease quantities of substances used or improve production-process efficiency to minimise pollution impacts, then a pollution-related resource-efficiency opportunity may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: reduced substance use; process efficiency; emission reduction; production optimisation; pollution minimisation; resource efficiency; safe alternatives

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential cost savings, productivity improvements, reduced compliance or remediation costs, and effects on financial performance and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the feasibility and likelihood of reducing substance quantities or improving process efficiency.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: resource efficiency: decrease quantities of substances used or improve efficiency of production process to minimise impacts.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show scope to diversify business activities through pollution prevention or control, then a pollution-related market opportunity may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: business diversification; new markets; lower-impact products; pollution-control services; safe and sustainable alternatives; changing demand

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential revenue, market access, margins, and cash-flow effects from diversified activities related to pollution prevention and control.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess market demand, technical feasibility, and the likelihood of successful diversification.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: markets: e.g., diversification of business activities.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that pollution prevention or control activities could qualify the undertaking for green funds, bonds, or loans, then a pollution-related financing opportunity may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: green funds; green bonds; green loans; sustainable finance; pollution-control investment; eligible environmental project; financing access

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential financing availability, financing cost, investment capacity, and effects on financial position and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess eligibility, investor or lender demand, and the likelihood of obtaining green finance.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: financing: e.g., access to green funds, bonds or loans.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show potential to diversify substances used or control emissions through innovation or technology, then a pollution-related resilience opportunity may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: substance diversification; alternative substances; emission-control technology; innovation; process technology; resilient supply; transition away from hazardous substances

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential avoided disruption and input volatility, reduced pollution costs, operational resilience, and effects on financial performance and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess technical feasibility and the likelihood that diversification or emission-control innovation will strengthen resilience.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: resilience: e.g., diversification of substances used and control of emissions through innovation or technology.

E2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show a proactive stance on pollution-risk management that can strengthen stakeholder relations, then a pollution-related reputational opportunity may be relevant.
E2_rules.identification_cues: proactive pollution management; stakeholder relations; community engagement; customer trust; pollution prevention leadership; consultation; reputation
E2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Undertaking, customers, affected communities, investors, wider society

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects of stronger stakeholder relations on demand, financing, licence to operate, financial performance, and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess the credibility of the proactive stance and the likelihood that it will improve stakeholder relations.

E2_rules.source_excerpt: reputation: positive stakeholder relations as a result of a proactive stance on managing risks.

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show material consumption of surface water or groundwater in activities, products or services, especially in areas at water risk or high water stress, then an actual or potential negative impact on available water resources may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: surface water consumption; groundwater consumption; water-intensive activities, products or services; total water consumption; water intensity; water-risk area; high-water-stress site; river basin
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Water bodies, aquatic ecosystems, affected communities and other users of shared water resources

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the volume and intensity of water consumed and the resulting pressure on available water resources.
impact_materiality.scope: Consider affected river basins and locations across own operations and the upstream and downstream value chain, prioritising water-risk areas.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Consider whether depleted surface water or groundwater can be restored and the time required for replenishment.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, assess the likelihood using consumption patterns, basin conditions and water-stress exposure.

E3_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E3 paragraphs 2, 12(c), 28(a)-(b), 29; AR 4(a), AR 5(b), AR 8(c)
E3_rules.source_excerpt: water, which encompasses the consumption of surface water, groundwater, as well as withdrawals and discharges of water

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show withdrawals of water from surface water, groundwater, polluted soils or aquifers, then an actual or potential negative impact on water quantity or the status of water bodies may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: water withdrawal; surface water abstraction; groundwater abstraction; aquifer; polluted soil water; remediation withdrawal; reduced water availability; withdrawal target
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Surface water bodies, groundwater bodies, aquatic ecosystems, affected communities and other water users

impact_materiality.scale: Assess withdrawal volumes and their effect on water quantity and water-body status.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess affected basins and value-chain locations, with particular attention to water-risk areas.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Consider aquifer or basin replenishment rates and whether ecological status can be restored.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, assess expected withdrawals against local water availability.

E3_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E3 AR 4(a), AR 17(e), AR 23(a), AR 24, AR 26
E3_rules.source_excerpt: The undertaking may provide targets relating to: (a) the reduction of water withdrawals

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show water discharges, reinjection, soakaway flows or activities that deteriorate water quality, then an actual or potential negative impact on surface water, groundwater or aquatic ecosystems may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: water discharge; groundwater discharge; aquifer reinjection; soakaway; swale; deteriorating water quality; water-body status; aquatic environment; discharge target
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Surface and groundwater bodies, aquatic ecosystems, human health, affected communities and biodiversity

impact_materiality.scale: Assess discharge quantity and the change in ecological or chemical water quality.
impact_materiality.scope: Consider all receiving water bodies, connected ecosystems and exposed communities.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess the feasibility and time needed to remediate contaminated or degraded water bodies.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, assess discharge frequency, controls and receiving-water vulnerability.

E3_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E3 paragraphs 12(a)(iii); AR 4(a), AR 17(a), AR 18(a), AR 23(b), AR 25-26
E3_rules.source_excerpt: prevent further deterioration and protect and enhance the status of water bodies and aquatic ecosystems

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show actions that avoid or reduce water use, improve water efficiency, treat water for sustainable sourcing, or reclaim, recycle and reuse water, then an actual or potential positive impact on water-resource availability may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: avoid water use; water efficiency; low-water process; water treatment; sustainable sourcing; reclaimed water; recycled water; reused water; reduced withdrawals; reduced consumption
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Water bodies, aquatic ecosystems, affected communities and other users of shared water resources

impact_materiality.scale: Assess absolute and intensity-based reductions in consumption or withdrawals and increases in recycled or reused water.
impact_materiality.scope: Consider benefits across affected basins and relevant own-operation and value-chain locations.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Not a severity criterion for positive impacts; assess instead whether benefits are durable and maintain water-resource functionality.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For planned actions, assess the likelihood that measures achieve the stated water savings.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: Resources can be allocated to: (a) avoid the use ... (b) reduce the use ... (c) reclaiming and reuse of water

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show protection, restoration or regeneration of water bodies, aquatic ecosystems, freshwater habitats or marine habitats, then an actual or potential positive impact on water and marine resources may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: water-body restoration; aquatic ecosystem regeneration; freshwater habitat restoration; marine habitat restoration; ecological status improvement; chemical quality improvement; groundwater quantity improvement
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Water bodies, aquatic ecosystems, marine ecosystems, biodiversity and affected communities

impact_materiality.scale: Assess improvements in ecological or chemical status, habitat condition and ecosystem functionality.
impact_materiality.scope: Consider the geographic area, water bodies, habitats and communities benefiting from restoration.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Not a severity criterion for positive impacts; assess the durability of restoration and risk of reversal.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For planned restoration, assess delivery probability and evidence that ecological outcomes will occur.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: restoration and regeneration of aquatic ecosystem and water bodies

E3_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Extraction and use of marine resources
E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show extraction or use of marine resources or material use of marine-resource commodities such as gravel, deep-sea minerals or seafood, then an actual or potential negative impact on marine-resource condition or availability may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: marine resource extraction; marine resource use; gravel; deep-sea minerals; seafood; marine commodity; fisheries; blue economy; pressure on marine resources
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Marine ecosystems, marine species, fishing communities, affected communities and users of marine resources

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the nature and quantity of commodities used and the pressure placed on marine resources.
impact_materiality.scope: Consider extraction areas, marine waters, affected species and relevant value-chain activities.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess recovery times and whether depleted resources or damaged habitats can be restored.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, assess sourcing volumes, extraction practices and resource condition.

E3_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E3 paragraph 3, 23(b); AR 4(b), AR 10-11, AR 15(b)
E3_rules.source_excerpt: marine resources, which encompasses the extraction and use of such resources and associated economic activities

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show fishing activity involving mobile bottom trawling, then an actual or potential negative impact on the seabed may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: mobile bottom trawling; bottom trawl; fishing activity; seabed disturbance; seabed damage; seafood sourcing; commercial fishing
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Seabed habitats, marine ecosystems, marine species and communities dependent on marine resources

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the intensity of seabed disturbance and resulting habitat damage.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the seabed area and marine species or ecosystem services affected.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Consider habitat recovery potential and the time required for seabed restoration.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, assess the frequency and location of bottom-trawling activity.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: fishing activity that involves mobile bottom trawling, which can also have negative impacts on the seabed

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that water or marine-resource impacts attributable to the undertaking affect local communities, water supply or human health, then an actual or potential negative impact on affected communities may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: affected community consultation; community water access; local water supply; human health; shared resource conflict; community complaint; stakeholder concern; community impact
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: Affected communities, including communities dependent on local water and marine resources

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the seriousness of effects on health, water access, livelihoods and community well-being.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the number and geographic distribution of affected communities and resource users.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Consider whether access, health, livelihood or environmental losses can be restored.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, use community consultation and local resource conditions to assess likelihood.

E3_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS E3 paragraphs 5, 8(b); AR 18(a), AR 18(c), AR 20
E3_rules.source_excerpt: The undertaking's impacts on water and marine resources affect people and communities.

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show operations, suppliers or downstream activities in locations exposed to water scarcity, water stress or high water stress, especially where the company depends on water, then a physical risk of constrained or interrupted operations may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: water scarcity; water stress; high-water-stress area; water-risk site; water dependency; constrained supply; operational interruption; river-basin exposure
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking, suppliers, customers, workers and communities sharing the affected water resource

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential effects on financial position, performance and cash flows, including disruption, higher costs and stranded or unusable facilities across short, medium and long horizons.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess basin stress, company water dependency, location exposure and operational resilience.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: identify physical risk including water quantity (water scarcity, water stress)

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show dependence on water of sufficient quality in locations where water-body quality is poor or deteriorating, then a physical risk to operations, costs or supply may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: poor water quality; deteriorating water body; treatment requirement; contaminated supply; water-quality dependency; operational constraint; basin status
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking, suppliers, customers and communities dependent on the affected water body

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess treatment costs, production constraints, supply disruption and effects on financial position, performance and cash flows across relevant horizons.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess water-body status, dependency on required quality and availability of substitutes or treatment.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: identify physical risk including ... water quality

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show dependence on ageing, decaying or unreliable water infrastructure, then a physical risk of disruption, leakage, reduced supply or additional expenditure may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: infrastructure decay; ageing pipeline; stormwater drain rehabilitation; unreliable water infrastructure; leakage; pipeline investment; supply interruption
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking, suppliers, customers, workers and affected communities

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess repair and capital costs, operational downtime and effects on financial performance and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess infrastructure condition, failure history, maintenance plans and dependency on the infrastructure.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: identify physical risk including ... infrastructure decay

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show dependence on commercially exploited fish, shellfish or other marine commodities whose availability is declining, then a physical risk of supply shortage or inability to operate in certain locations may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: fish dependency; shellfish dependency; seafood sourcing; species rarefaction; declining fish stock; unavailable marine commodity; supply shortage; geographic operating constraint
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking, suppliers, customers, fishing communities and marine-resource-dependent workers

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess lost revenue, input-price increases, substitution costs and inability to operate in affected areas.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess resource condition, sourcing concentration, exploitation pressure and availability of substitute commodities.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: unavailability of some marine resources-related commodities (e.g. the rarefaction of some species of fish)

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show material exposure to stronger water protection, water-quality requirements or regulation of water-supply flows, then a policy or legal transition risk may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: new water regulation; stronger water protection; water-quality regulation; regulated supply flows; permit change; compliance expenditure; regulatory exposure
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking and value-chain partners subject to water or marine regulation

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess compliance costs, capital requirements, operating constraints and effects on financial performance and cash flows.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess regulatory developments, geographic exposure and the gap between current practices and expected requirements.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: introduction of regulation or policy ... increased water protection, increased quality of water regulations, regulation of flows of water supply

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show dependence on water bodies or marine resources subject to ineffective governance, particularly transboundary governance and cooperation, then a transition risk from resource degradation or allocation uncertainty may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: ineffective water governance; marine-resource governance; transboundary basin; cross-border cooperation; allocation uncertainty; shared resource; water degradation; ocean degradation
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking, value-chain partners, governments and communities sharing transboundary resources

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess disruption, access constraints, conflict-related costs and effects of resource degradation.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess governance effectiveness, cross-border coordination and the undertaking's dependency on the shared resource.

E3_rules.source_excerpt: ineffective governance of water bodies or marine resources, in particular across boundaries

E3_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show non-respect of water permits or allocations, or negligence toward or killing of threatened marine species, then a policy and legal risk of sanctions or litigation may be relevant.
E3_rules.identification_cues: permit breach; allocation breach; non-compliance; threatened marine species; species mortality; negligence; sanction; fine; litigation; legal claim
E3_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking, regulators, affected communities, marine species and value-chain partners

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess potential fines, damages, legal costs, operating restrictions and reputational spillovers.

S1_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking; employees and non-employees participating in transition-related job creation or skills programmes

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess the potential financial benefit through access to qualified labour, reputation, customer appeal, market differentiation, productivity, operational resilience, or successful just transition.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on whether relevant policies, actions, resources, targets, workforce coverage, and external market or regulatory conditions support the opportunity.

S1_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS S1, paragraph 14(e); AR 7; AR 10; AR 43
S1_rules.source_excerpt: Impacts, risks and opportunities include restructuring and employment loss as well as opportunities arising from job creation and reskilling or upskilling; opportunities... may result from providing opportunities for the workforce such as job creation and upskilling in the context of a “just transition”.

S1_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Decent pay and conditions for non-employees
S1_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show guarantees of decent pay and conditions for non-employees in the own workforce, then opportunities may be relevant through market differentiation and greater customer appeal.
S1_rules.identification_cues: decent pay; decent conditions; non-employees; contractors; employment agencies; self-employed people; market differentiation; customer appeal; sustainable goods; ethically sourced goods
S1_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking; non-employees benefiting from decent pay and conditions

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess the potential financial benefit through access to qualified labour, reputation, customer appeal, market differentiation, productivity, operational resilience, or successful just transition.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on whether relevant policies, actions, resources, targets, workforce coverage, and external market or regulatory conditions support the opportunity.

S1_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS S1, AR 44(c); paragraphs 53-56; paragraph 71
S1_rules.source_excerpt: Opportunities related to the undertaking’s impacts on its own workforce may include market differentiation and greater customer appeal from guaranteeing decent pay and conditions for non-employees.

S1_rules.esrs_subtopic: Equal treatment and opportunities for all
S1_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Training, skills development and workforce capability
S1_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show skills audits, training to fill skills gaps, reskilling or upskilling programmes, then opportunities may be relevant through improved workforce capability and reduced dependency-related risks.
S1_rules.identification_cues: skills audits; training to fill skills gaps; reskilling; upskilling; training programmes; career development; qualified labour; employability; workforce capability; skills development
S1_rules.affected_stakeholders: The undertaking; employees and non-employees whose skills support operations

financial_materiality.magnitude: Assess the potential financial benefit through access to qualified labour, reputation, customer appeal, market differentiation, productivity, operational resilience, or successful just transition.
financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on whether relevant policies, actions, resources, targets, workforce coverage, and external market or regulatory conditions support the opportunity.

S1_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS S1, paragraph 14(e); paragraphs 81-85; AR 7; Appendix A.3
S1_rules.source_excerpt: Opportunities... may result from providing opportunities for the workforce such as job creation and upskilling in the context of a “just transition”; Skills audits, training to fill skills gaps.

S1_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Severe human rights incidents and complaints
S1_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show lawsuits, formal complaints, serious public allegations, media reports, fines, penalties or compensation connected to the undertaking’s own workforce, then actual severe negative human rights impacts may be relevant.
S1_rules.identification_cues: severe human rights incidents; lawsuits; formal complaints; public reports; media allegations; National Contact Points; fines; penalties; compensation; remediation plans; incidents reviewed; complaints; non-respect of UN Guiding Principles; ILO Declaration; OECD Guidelines
S1_rules.affected_stakeholders: Employees and non-employees in the undertaking’s own workforce affected by severe human rights incidents or complaints

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the severity of harm to labour rights, human rights, income security, health and safety, dignity, equality, or privacy of affected own workforce members.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess how widespread the impact is across employees, non-employees, sites, countries, worker categories, or vulnerable groups.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess the difficulty of remedying the harm, considering whether it involves severe human rights impacts, health injury, fatalities, discrimination, loss of income, or long-term career effects.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood using evidence of incidents, complaints, workforce composition, high-risk operations/geographies, missing controls, worker characteristics, employment practices, and business pressures.

S1_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS S1, paragraphs 100-104; AR 103-106
S1_rules.source_excerpt: The undertaking shall disclose the number of work-related incidents and/or complaints and severe human rights impacts within its own workforce... Severe human rights incidents include instances of lawsuits, formal complaints through the undertaking or third-party complaint mechanisms, serious allegations in public reports or the media.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Working conditions
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Secure employment, working time, adequate wage, work-life balance
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show reliance on upstream, downstream, outsourced, joint venture, special purpose vehicle, or other non-own-workforce workers whose employment security, working time, wages, or work-life balance may be affected by the undertaking’s operations, products, services, or business relationships, then negative impacts on value chain workers’ working conditions may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: value chain workers; outsourced services; supplier workers; downstream workers; franchisees; retailers; logistics providers; joint venture workers; special purpose vehicle workers; insecure employment; temporary work; limited-hours contracts; working time; overtime; adequate wage; living wage; work-life balance; purchasing practices; supplier labour conditions
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Workers in the undertaking’s upstream and downstream value chain who are outside the own workforce, including supplier, logistics, distribution, franchisee, retailer, outsourced service, joint venture, and deeper supply chain workers.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how serious the working-condition impact is for affected workers, including wage adequacy, employment security, working time and work-life balance.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the impact affects individual workers, specific sites or supplier groups, or is widespread across value chain contexts or relationships.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess how difficult it would be to restore adequate working conditions or compensate affected workers.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential impacts, assess whether the company’s value chain arrangements make such working-condition impacts likely.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: The Standard covers workers in the upstream and downstream value chain who are or can be materially impacted; material impacts may relate to working conditions such as secure employment, working time, adequate wage and work-life balance.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Working conditions
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Health and safety
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show value chain workers exposed to unsafe workplaces, industrial accidents, oil spills, severe health crises, chemical handling, hazardous equipment, or other occupational health and safety conditions connected with the undertaking, then negative health and safety impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: health and safety; occupational safety; industrial accident; oil spill; pandemic; severe health crisis; workers handling chemicals; workers operating equipment; supplier site safety; maintenance workers; delivery workers; workplace injury; hazardous work; safety incidents
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers exposed to occupational health and safety risks, including supplier workers, outsourced service workers, maintenance workers, logistics and distribution workers, and workers in deeper supply chains.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the seriousness of injury, illness or exposure for affected workers.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the number and categories of workers exposed and whether the issue is incident-specific or systemic.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether harm can be remedied through medical care, compensation, workplace correction, or other remediation.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess the probability of health and safety impacts based on hazardous tasks, equipment, substances, crisis exposure, or incident history.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Working conditions include health and safety; material negative impacts may be related to individual incidents such as an industrial accident or an oil spill, and some activities such as handling chemicals or operating equipment may put workers at risk.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Working conditions
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Social dialogue, freedom of association and collective bargaining
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that value chain workers’ social dialogue, freedom of association, works council participation, collective bargaining, or trade union activity may be restricted or insufficiently respected in connection with the undertaking’s value chain, then negative labour-rights impacts may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: social dialogue; freedom of association; collective bargaining; works councils; trade unions; trade unionists; global union federation; global framework agreement; worker representatives; supplier code; labour rights; retaliation against union activity
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers and their legitimate representatives, including trade unionists and workers in supplier, downstream, franchise, logistics, and other business relationship contexts.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the severity of restrictions on collective worker rights and representation.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the issue affects specific worker groups, sites, countries, suppliers, or whole value chain contexts.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether workers can regain access to representation, bargaining, and remedy without retaliation.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess the likelihood based on country context, business relationships, supplier policies, and worker-representation evidence.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Working conditions include social dialogue, freedom of association, works councils and collective bargaining; the undertaking may have agreements related to respect of human rights of workers in the value chain, including their right to bargain collectively.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Equal treatment and opportunities for all
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Gender equality, equal pay, disability inclusion and diversity
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show discrimination, unequal treatment, unequal pay, lack of disability inclusion, or exclusion of diverse groups among value chain workers connected with the undertaking’s value chain, then negative impacts on equal treatment and opportunities may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: gender equality; equal pay; equal pay for work of equal value; disability inclusion; diversity; women workers; migrant workers; young workers; workers with disabilities; discrimination; terms and conditions; inclusion; supplier employment practices
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers who may experience unequal treatment or reduced opportunities, including women workers, migrant workers, young workers, workers with disabilities, and other diverse or marginalised groups.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how significantly unequal treatment affects workers’ income, employment conditions, dignity, safety or access to opportunity.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the issue affects particular worker groups, factories, suppliers, countries or broader value chain contexts.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether affected workers can obtain remedy, equalisation of treatment, or restoration of opportunities.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood using evidence on workforce demographics, supplier practices, country contexts and vulnerable-group exposure.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Equal treatment and opportunities include gender equality, equal pay for work of equal value, employment and inclusion of persons with disabilities and diversity; women workers may face discrimination in terms and conditions of work.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Equal treatment and opportunities for all
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Violence and harassment in the workplace
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show violence, harassment, sexual harassment, or insufficient measures against harassment in workplaces where value chain workers are employed or contracted, then negative impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: violence; harassment; sexual harassment; workplace harassment; measures against violence and harassment; grievance mechanisms; worker complaints; supplier workplace conduct; women workers; vulnerable workers
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers exposed to violence or harassment, particularly vulnerable or marginalised workers such as women workers, migrant workers and workers with disabilities.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the seriousness of harm to workers’ safety, dignity and wellbeing.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether incidents are isolated or indicate a broader workplace or value chain pattern.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether effective remedy, protection from retaliation and prevention of recurrence are available.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on worker complaints, workplace context, vulnerable groups, and availability of trusted channels.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Equal treatment and opportunities include measures against violence and harassment in the workplace; programmes may result in reports of reduced sexual harassment in the workplace.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Equal treatment and opportunities for all
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Training and skills development
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that value chain workers lack access to training, skills development, or upskilling where such access is relevant to their work or transition-related employability, then negative impacts on equal opportunities for value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: training; skills development; upskilling; capacity building; supplier workforce; just transition; job skills; worker development; access to training; women workers; young workers
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers whose access to training, skills development or upskilling may affect their employment opportunities, including supplier, downstream and transition-affected workers.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how strongly lack of training or skills development affects workers’ opportunities and employability.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the issue concerns specific worker groups or is widespread across suppliers, regions or activities.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether lost opportunities can be remediated through later training, job access or support programmes.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on business changes, transition plans, skills requirements and training availability.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Equal treatment and opportunities include training and skills development; positive impacts may include job creation and upskilling in the context of a just transition.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Other work-related rights
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Child labour
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show sourcing, production, commodities, countries, regions, or business relationships where there is a significant risk of child labour among workers in the value chain, then negative child-labour impacts may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: child labour; young workers; commodity supply chain; high-risk country; high-risk region; harvesting commodities; mining; supplier code of conduct; due diligence; upstream sourcing; forced labour and child labour risk; vulnerable workers
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Children or young workers in the undertaking’s upstream, downstream, or deeper value chain who may be affected by child labour risks.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the severity of harm to children’s rights, development, education and wellbeing.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the risk is specific to incidents or widespread/systemic in commodities, countries, regions or supplier networks.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess how difficult it is to remediate the harm and restore affected children’s rights and opportunities.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on country, commodity, supplier, sourcing and due diligence evidence.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Other work-related rights include child labour; the undertaking shall disclose geographies or commodities for which there is a significant risk of child labour among workers in the value chain.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Other work-related rights
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Forced labour, compulsory labour and human trafficking
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show forced labour, compulsory labour, human trafficking, recruitment fees, poorly regulated labour supply, or sourcing from geographies or commodities with significant forced labour risk, then negative impacts on value chain workers’ fundamental rights may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: forced labour; compulsory labour; human trafficking; trafficking in human beings; recruitment fees; migrant workers; poorly regulated labour supply; supplier code; responsible recruitment; commodity supply chain; import restrictions; worker coercion; labour broker
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers exposed to forced labour, compulsory labour, trafficking or recruitment-fee practices, especially migrant workers and workers in high-risk countries, commodities or supplier networks.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the severity of infringement of workers’ fundamental rights and freedom.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the issue is incident-specific or systemic in particular countries, commodities, sectors or supplier relationships.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess the difficulty of freeing workers from coercion, reimbursing fees, restoring rights and preventing recurrence.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on migrant labour, recruitment practices, country or commodity risk, and supplier due diligence.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Other work-related rights include forced labour; policies shall state whether they explicitly address trafficking in human beings, forced labour or compulsory labour and child labour.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Other work-related rights
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Adequate housing, water and sanitation
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show that value chain workers’ work or living arrangements connected with the undertaking involve inadequate housing, water, or sanitation, then negative impacts on value chain workers’ work-related rights may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: adequate housing; worker accommodation; dormitory; water; sanitation; migrant worker housing; supplier accommodation; labour camps; living conditions; worker welfare; basic services
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers whose employment or contracted work is linked to housing, water or sanitation conditions, including migrant workers, supplier workers and outsourced workers.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the seriousness of inadequate housing, water or sanitation for workers’ health, dignity and rights.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess how many workers and sites are affected and whether conditions are systemic in a supplier, region or activity.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess the feasibility and timeliness of remedying living conditions and any related harm.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on worker accommodation arrangements, migration status, supplier practices and country context.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Other work-related rights include adequate housing, water and sanitation.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Other work-related rights
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Privacy
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show data use, monitoring, grievance channels, or other processes involving value chain workers’ personal information in ways that may affect privacy, then negative privacy impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: privacy; data use; worker data; monitoring; surveillance; grievance mechanism data; confidential complaints; anonymous complaints; personal information; data protection; supplier worker records; retaliation protection
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers whose privacy may be affected by company, supplier, third-party, or grievance-channel data practices.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the seriousness of privacy infringement and consequences for workers, including retaliation or misuse of sensitive information.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether affected data practices apply to individual complaints, specific worker groups or broader worker populations.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether privacy harm can be corrected, information protected, or consequences remediated.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on the company’s data use, monitoring, grievance mechanisms, confidentiality controls and supplier practices.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Other work-related rights include privacy; the undertaking shall disclose whether it avoids negative impacts through its own practices, including data use, and may describe confidentiality, privacy and data protection in grievance mechanisms.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Vulnerable value chain workers
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Particular characteristics, contexts or activities
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show value chain workers who are particularly vulnerable because of inherent characteristics, marginalised status, work context, or hazardous activities, then heightened negative impacts on those worker groups may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: vulnerable workers; trade unionists; migrant workers; home workers; women workers; young workers; workers with disabilities; low-paid workers; zero-hours contracts; recruitment fees; chemical handling; equipment operation; poorly regulated labour market; marginalised workers
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Particularly vulnerable value chain workers, including trade unionists, migrant workers, home workers, women workers, young workers, workers with disabilities, low-paid workers and workers undertaking hazardous activities.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess whether vulnerability increases the severity of harm for affected worker groups.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether vulnerability is limited to specific groups, factories, countries, activities or broader value chain contexts.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether affected vulnerable workers can access effective remedy and protection without retaliation or exclusion.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood using evidence on worker characteristics, working contexts, activities, and country or labour market conditions.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: The undertaking shall describe workers who are particularly vulnerable to negative impacts, such as trade unionists, migrant workers, home workers, women or young workers, and how workers with particular characteristics or activities may be at greater risk of harm.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Working conditions
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Business model pressure on labour rights
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show a value proposition or business model based on lowest-cost products, high-speed delivery, or similar commercial pressures that may put pressure on labour rights in upstream or downstream value chains, then negative impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: lowest cost products; cheapest prices; high-speed delivery; fast delivery; price pressure; labour rights; purchasing practices; supplier margins; delivery workforce; upstream labour; downstream labour; supplier pressure; labour cost reduction
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers in upstream and downstream entities affected by business-model or value-proposition pressures, including supplier, delivery, logistics, distribution and retail workers.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how commercial pressure affects workers’ labour rights, pay, working hours, safety or employment conditions.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether the pressure affects specific suppliers or broad upstream/downstream labour contexts.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether impacts can be mitigated through changed purchasing, delivery, pricing or other internal practices.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on evidence of low-price strategy, delivery speed targets, procurement practices and supplier labour conditions.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Impacts may relate to the undertaking’s value proposition, such as providing lowest cost products or services, or high-speed delivery, in ways that put pressure on labour rights in the upstream and downstream value chains.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Value chain transparency and sourcing
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Unclear provenance and deeper supply chains
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show reliance on commodities, components, suppliers, or deeper supply chains of unclear provenance or limited visibility, then negative impacts on workers in those upstream value chains may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: unclear provenance; limited visibility; deeper supply chain; commodities; extraction; metals; minerals; harvesting commodities; refining; manufacturing; processing; supplier traceability; opaque sourcing; components; supplier mapping
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Workers deeper in the supply chain, including commodity extraction, harvesting, refining, manufacturing and processing workers whose conditions may be affected but not directly visible to the undertaking.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the severity of potential worker impacts in less visible upstream activities.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess how many tiers, commodities, countries, suppliers or worker groups may be affected.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether lack of visibility makes remediation, prevention or worker remedy more difficult.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on supply chain opacity, commodity risks, traceability gaps and sourcing context.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Value chain workers include those involved in extraction, harvesting, refining, manufacturing or other processing, and workers deeper in the supply chain; impacts may relate to relying on commodities of unclear provenance without visibility on impacts on workers.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Working conditions
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Subcontracting, precarious work and informal work
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show subcontracting, third-party employment, informal workers, short-term or limited-hours contracts, or shifted inventory risk to suppliers linked to the undertaking’s sourcing or business model, then negative impacts on value chain workers’ labour rights and working conditions may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: sub-contracting; subcontracting to third parties; third-party employment; informal workers; precarious work; short-term contracts; limited hours contracts; inventory risk; supplier risk shifting; supplier code; procurement practices; responsible sourcing; supplier labour
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Workers employed through suppliers, subcontractors, third parties or informal arrangements in the undertaking’s value chain.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how precarious or indirect work arrangements affect workers’ security, wages, rights and access to remedy.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether such arrangements are isolated or widespread across suppliers, subcontractors or sourcing regions.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether workers can be identified, reached and remediated despite indirect or informal arrangements.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on subcontracting models, procurement pressure, supplier codes and labour arrangements.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Impacts may relate to the cost structure and revenue model, such as shifting inventory risk to suppliers, and supplier codes may address precarious work, third-party employment, sub-contracting or informal workers.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Just transition
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Transition-related impacts on value chain workers
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show innovation, restructuring, mine closures, increased mining of transition minerals, solar panel production, or other changes linked to transition to greener or climate-neutral operations, then negative transition-related impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: just transition; greener operations; climate-neutral operations; innovation; restructuring; closure of mines; mining of transition minerals; minerals needed for sustainable economy; solar panel production; transition supply chain; job losses; worker displacement; supplier transition
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers affected by transition-related restructuring, closures, new production processes, or increased extraction and production activities.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the seriousness of transition-related effects on workers’ livelihoods, safety, rights and employment opportunities.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess whether impacts affect specific operations, commodities, suppliers, geographies or wider transition supply chains.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Assess whether impacts can be mitigated through worker engagement, retraining, remedy, or responsible transition planning.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on transition plans, restructuring, supply chain shifts and transition-related sourcing.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Consideration includes impacts on value chain workers that may arise from the transition to greener and climate-neutral operations, including innovation, restructuring, mine closures, increased mining of minerals and solar panel production.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Positive impacts on value chain workers
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Purchasing practices and capacity-building
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show updated purchasing practices, supplier capacity-building, responsible sourcing, or engagement with value chain entities designed to improve worker outcomes, then positive impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: updated purchasing practices; responsible sourcing; capacity-building; supplier training; worker rights training; commercial leverage; incentives; supplier support; improving working conditions; adequate wage; worker outcomes; positive impact initiatives
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Supplier workers and other value chain workers who may benefit from improved purchasing practices, capacity-building or worker-rights initiatives.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the significance of intended or achieved improvements in workers’ conditions, rights or wellbeing.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess how many workers, suppliers, regions or worker groups benefit.
impact_materiality.likelihood: For potential positive impacts, assess whether planned practices or programmes are likely to deliver worker outcomes.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Positive impacts may result from updated purchasing practices or capacity-building to supply chain workers; actions may include purchasing practices, capacity-building or other engagement with value chain entities.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Positive impacts on value chain workers
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Job creation and upskilling in a just transition
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show job creation, upskilling, training, or workforce opportunity programmes for value chain workers in the context of a just transition, then positive impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: job creation; upskilling; training; skills development; just transition; transition jobs; supplier workforce; delivery jobs; capacity-building; workforce opportunities; women delivery jobs; sustainable economy
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers who may gain jobs, skills or improved opportunities through transition-related programmes, including supplier, downstream and underrepresented workers.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how materially the programme improves workers’ employment, skills or opportunity outcomes.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the number of workers, worker groups, suppliers, regions or value chain segments benefiting.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess whether programme design, resources and worker engagement make the positive outcomes likely.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Not applicable in the same way as for negative impacts; assess whether employment and skills outcomes are sustained and evidenced as worker outcomes rather than training activity alone.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Positive impacts may include providing opportunities for the workforce such as job creation and upskilling in the context of a just transition; training may increase the proportion of women able to take delivery jobs.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Positive impacts on value chain workers
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Financial literacy and worker support programmes
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show active support programmes for value chain workers, such as financial literacy initiatives, that are intended to improve workers’ capabilities or wellbeing, then positive impacts on value chain workers may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: financial literacy; worker support programme; active support programme; household budgets; savings goals; women workers; promotion; reduced sexual harassment; worker wellbeing; capability-building; supplier worker programme
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Value chain workers participating in support or financial literacy programmes, including women workers and other groups targeted by worker support initiatives.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess the importance of improved worker capability, financial wellbeing or related workplace outcomes.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess the number and types of workers reached and whether outcomes are observed across sites or worker groups.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess whether programme evidence shows actual worker outcomes rather than only activity completion.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Not applicable in the same way as for negative impacts; assess whether the programme delivers actual outcomes for workers rather than evidence of activities alone.

S2_rules.source_excerpt: Respect for workers’ rights and active support programmes, for example financial literacy initiatives, can bring business opportunities; disclosures may distinguish activities from actual outcomes for workers.

S2_rules.esrs_subtopic: Positive impacts on value chain workers
S2_rules.esrs_sub_subtopic: Adequate wage and income improvements
S2_rules.rule_statement: If company documents show initiatives to ensure adequate wages, decent pay, income improvements, or smallholder earnings in the value chain, then positive impacts on value chain workers’ livelihoods may be relevant.
S2_rules.identification_cues: adequate wage; living wage; decent pay; income increase; smallholder farmers; supplier wages; responsible purchasing; sustainable supply; commodity farmers; capacity-building; worker income; maintaining income while reducing overtime
S2_rules.affected_stakeholders: Supplier workers, smallholder farmers and other value chain workers whose livelihoods may improve through wage, income or purchasing initiatives.

impact_materiality.scale: Assess how substantially income, wage adequacy or livelihood security improves for workers.
impact_materiality.scope: Assess how many workers, smallholders, suppliers, crops or regions are affected.
impact_materiality.likelihood: Assess whether purchasing, wage or income measures are likely to deliver sustained improvements.
impact_materiality.irremediability: Not applicable in the same way as for negative impacts; assess whether wage and income gains support sustained livelihoods and a future sustainable supply.

S2_rules.esrs_reference: ESRS S2 para 2(a); AR 30, AR 37, AR 40(d), AR 46

financial_materiality.likelihood: Assess likelihood based on sourcing geographies, commodities, supplier due diligence, allegations, reported incidents and applicable laws.
